headline: Yesterday's 1:15 buyer at 355 Comanche wrote an offer the same afternoon — it dies at 7 PM tonight — and a second buyer walks 195 Lake View at 3:00 today while that seller still hasn't heard from you in six days.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 SHE WROTE THE OFFER. Cassie C. (RE/MAX Advantage) toured at 1:15 yesterday and filed her feedback at 5:23 PM: 'Is your client interested in this listing? Yes' — and under what made the client want the home, she wrote 'Writing up an offer!' She also marked the price 'too high.' Both are true at once and together they ARE the negotiation: they want the house and they are at their cash ceiling, not their interest ceiling. The written offer followed four minutes later and VOIDS AT 7:00 PM TONIGHT.
hotSignals.action: Call Seth B. this morning, not this afternoon. Lead with her own words off the feedback form — 'writing up an offer' is not a buyer looking for a discount, it's a buyer at their limit. The counter recommendation, net sheet and comps are already staged as a Gmail draft; send it the moment he says go. Countering also voids their 7 PM clock and hands the clock to you. ⚠️ One thing to confirm first and it is worth real money: whether the earlier ARC Realty offer is still live. If it is, Seth is CHOOSING between two offers, and the new offer's home-sale contingency is exactly the weakness the other side may not carry.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 A SECOND BUYER WALKS THE HOUSE AT 3:00 THIS AFTERNOON — showing #11, booked yesterday afternoon, Quin W. of EXIT Realty Southern Select. This is the third distinct buyer to walk this house in eight days while the conditional re-offer sits unanswered past the 96-hour mark, and your seller — who occupies the house — has heard nothing from you in six days.
hotSignals.action: Call before the appointment, not after. Today's showing is genuinely new information, which makes it the cleanest possible reason to break six days of silence without it feeling like a confession. Then use it where it pays: the re-offering buyers' own home is STILL not under contract and goes live tomorrow, so competing interest is the only lever that fixes that weakness — and it only works if the other side hears about it.

hotSignals.signal: 🟡 The permit got chased on a Saturday — the buyer's agent opened with 'I know we are on a time limit.' You closed both of Friday's promises yourself and produced the first date anyone has ever attached to the permit: the City of Hoover final is 'next week,' with a $50 item pre-conceded. The buyers are still described as very concerned and nothing has gone to them in writing.
hotSignals.action: 'Next week' is a status, not the closeout date this file needs — get the actual date from the seller and put it back to the buyer's agent in writing, so the buyers read it instead of hearing it thirdhand. Then call the written backup buyer, Kulsum B. (Keller Williams Hoover), who said 'interested: Yes' with no price objection and has now gone six days uncalled. A backup at or near list costs nothing and strengthens every answer you give on the repair request.
